summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (read-only standbys) on CentOS Stream 10, verified data propagation and standby write-rejection, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time node restart protocol (standbys first, primary last) with boot-identity and post-restart cluster health verification.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server/postgresql-contrib 16.14 on node1, node2, node3
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes
Initialized and configured node1 as primary (listen_addresses, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby, pg_hba.conf rules for replication and client access from 10.100.241.0/24)
Generated a replication role/password on node1 and moved it to node2/node3 via inter-node SSH (not through the tool transcript, aside from one incidental grep echo)
Ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 on node2 and node3 to build standbys with standby.signal and primary_conninfo auto-configured
Started PostgreSQL on standbys and verified pg_stat_replication shows both streaming, and pg_is_in_recovery()=t on both
Created repl_test table and inserted a row on primary; confirmed it appeared on both standbys and that standbys reject INSERTs (read-only)
Captured baseline boot_id on all three nodes
Rebooted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed postgresql active, in recovery, and prior data intact
Rebooted node3, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed postgresql active, in recovery, and prior data intact
Confirmed primary still shows both standbys streaming before restarting it

Rebooted node1 (primary) last, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, confirmed postgresql active and NOT in recovery (primary), inserted new row, confirmed both standbys reconnected as streaming and received the new row

evidence.requirement: Primary configured with replication-ready settings and replication role
evidence.summary: postgresql.conf and pg_hba.conf updated for replication; replicator role created; primary listening on 0.0.0.0:5432 after restart

evidence.requirement: Standbys built from primary via pg_basebackup and running in recovery
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup completed with -R on node2/node3 producing standby.signal and primary_conninfo; postgresql started and pg_is_in_recovery()=t on both
pg_stat_replication on node1 lists node2 and node3 as streaming/async

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 visible via SELECT on node2 and node3; standby INSERT attempts correctly rejected with read-only transaction error

evidence.requirement: Baseline boot identity captured for all nodes before restart
node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged, connection dropped mid-reboot, node2 boot_id changed to 179d0323..., postgresql active/in-recovery with repl_test data intact post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged, connection dropped mid-reboot, node3 boot_id changed to 53662e22..., postgresql active/in-recovery with repl_test data intact post-restart

evidence.requirement: Both standbys reconnected to primary before primary restart
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 confirms both node2 and node3 streaming again after their restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery as primary with replication resumed
evidence.summary: reboot acknowledged, connection dropped mid-reboot, node1 boot_id changed to 4a2c41f5..., postgresql active and pg_is_in_recovery()=f (writable primary), new row inserted post-restart and confirmed present on both standbys, pg_stat_replication shows both reconnected
